answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so k coordinated identities that equivocate create pairwise evidence and incur penalties scaling as O(k²), rather than merely k. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier compounds the swarm’s capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation limits recovery. A vine of aliases may seek nectar from separate rewards, but shared control leaves a relic of correlated proofs that exposes the group and puts its bonds at risk.
